Ruffley & Lutz et al. — statistics computed for the NEE revision

Flowering time × WUE (δ¹³C): correlations, slopes, covariances

2026-08-12

Everything below is recomputed from the deposited data. Written to answer Reviewer 2 comment 1 (“no p-value or r² values are listed”) and the related Reviewer 1 points on Fig. 3B/3C.

Each of the 29 edited lines comes from a distinct accession (no pseudo-replication), and all 29 have δ¹³C measured in triplicate. The 19 are the subset with a paired progenitor — not a measured-vs-imputed distinction.

firstnum <- function(v) as.numeric(sapply(v, function(x) {
  m <- regmatches(x, regexpr("[0-9]+", x)); if (length(m)) m else NA }))
c(edited_lines = nrow(E), unique_accessions = length(unique(firstnum(E$line))),
  all_measured_3reps = sum(E$deltaC_mean_count == 3),
  paired_subset_of_29 = all(pr$line %in% E$line))
##        edited_lines   unique_accessions  all_measured_3reps paired_subset_of_29 
##                  29                  29                  29                   1

Core statistics

stat <- function(x, y, label) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  ct <- cor.test(x, y); f <- lm(y ~ x)
  data.frame(set = label, n = length(x),
             r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3),
             p = signif(ct$p.value, 3),
             slope = round(unname(coef(f)[2]), 2),
             slope_SE = round(summary(f)$coef[2, 2], 2),
             cov = round(cov(x, y), 3),
             sd_d13C = round(sd(x), 3),
             sd_FT = round(sd(y), 2))
}

tab <- rbind(
  stat(pr$deltaC_mean_mean, pr$dag_mean,   "19 edited (paired w/ progenitor)"),
  stat(E$deltaC_mean_mean,  E$dag_mean,    "29 edited (all)"),
  stat(W$deltaC_mean_mean,  W$dag_mean,    "19 progenitors"),
  stat(WC$deltaC_mean_mean, WC$dag_mean,   "20 progenitors + Col-0"),
  stat(at16$Delta_13C,      at16$FT16,     "248 natural accessions (FT16)"),
  stat(at10$Delta_13C,      at10$FT10,     "261 natural accessions (FT10)"))
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE)

Flowering time is days-to-flowering at 21 °C for the chamber sets and FT10/FT16 for the natural accessions, so slopes are comparable in kind but not identical quantities.

20 progenitors + Col-0 reproduces the β = 10.44 ± 16.9 reported in the manuscript, confirming the Fig. 3B wild-type line includes Col-0.

Formal tests

fz <- function(r1, r2, n1, n2) {
  z <- (atanh(r1) - atanh(r2)) / sqrt(1/(n1 - 3) + 1/(n2 - 3))
  c(z = round(z, 3), p = round(2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z))), 4)) }

rbind(
  `edited vs natural (FT16)`  = fz(cor(E$deltaC_mean_mean, E$dag_mean),
                                   cor(at16$Delta_13C, at16$FT16), nrow(E), nrow(at16)),
  `edited vs natural (FT10)`  = fz(cor(E$deltaC_mean_mean, E$dag_mean),
                                   cor(at10$Delta_13C, at10$FT10), nrow(E), nrow(at10)),
  `edited vs progenitors+Col0`= fz(cor(E$deltaC_mean_mean, E$dag_mean),
                                   cor(WC$deltaC_mean_mean, WC$dag_mean), nrow(E), nrow(WC)))
##                                 z      p
## edited vs natural (FT16)   -0.033 0.9736
## edited vs natural (FT10)   -0.321 0.7482
## edited vs progenitors+Col0  0.802 0.4227
b <- rbind(data.frame(x = E$deltaC_mean_mean,  y = E$dag_mean,  g = "edited"),
           data.frame(x = WC$deltaC_mean_mean, y = WC$dag_mean, g = "progenitor"))
round(summary(lm(y ~ x * g, data = b))$coef, 4)   # interaction = slope difference
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
## (Intercept)   163.1935   264.8553  0.6162   0.5409
## x               4.5799     8.5963  0.5328   0.5968
## gprogenitor   223.1604   423.5029  0.5269   0.6008
## x:gprogenitor   5.8605    13.9030  0.4215   0.6754
cc <- function(s) cov(s$deltaC_mean_mean, s$dag_mean)
obs <- cc(E) - cc(WC)
boot <- replicate(20000, cc(E[sample(nrow(E), replace = TRUE), ]) -
                          cc(WC[sample(nrow(WC), replace = TRUE), ]))
c(observed_difference = round(obs, 3),
  CI_lower = round(quantile(boot, .025), 3), CI_upper = round(quantile(boot, .975), 3))
## observed_difference       CI_lower.2.5%      CI_upper.97.5% 
##              -0.974              -8.509               6.281

The variance test is the robust result. Editing collapses flowering-time variance ~32-fold while leaving δ¹³C variance untouched.

rbind(d13C = c(progenitors = var(WC$deltaC_mean_mean), edited = var(E$deltaC_mean_mean)),
      FT   = c(var(WC$dag_mean), var(E$dag_mean)))
##      progenitors     edited
## d13C   0.1796541  0.1969672
## FT   947.7433865 29.2977866
var.test(WC$dag_mean, E$dag_mean)
## 
##  F test to compare two variances
## 
## data:  WC$dag_mean and E$dag_mean
## F = 32.349, num df = 19, denom df = 28, p-value = 6.439e-14
## alternative hypothesis: true ratio of variances is not equal to 1
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  14.37375 77.98251
## sample estimates:
## ratio of variances 
##           32.34863

Box’s M tests the whole covariance matrix, so it rejects here because of the variance, not the covariance — do not cite it as evidence about covariance.

S1 <- cov(cbind(E$deltaC_mean_mean, E$dag_mean));  n1 <- nrow(E)
S2 <- cov(cbind(WC$deltaC_mean_mean, WC$dag_mean)); n2 <- nrow(WC); p <- 2; g <- 2
Sp <- ((n1-1)*S1 + (n2-1)*S2) / (n1 + n2 - g)
M  <- (n1+n2-g)*log(det(Sp)) - ((n1-1)*log(det(S1)) + (n2-1)*log(det(S2)))
cst <- 1 - (sum(1/c(n1-1, n2-1)) - 1/(n1+n2-g)) * (2*p^2+3*p-1) / (6*(p+1)*(g-1))
c(chi2 = round(M*cst, 2), df = (g-1)*p*(p+1)/2,
  p = signif(pchisq(M*cst, (g-1)*p*(p+1)/2, lower.tail = FALSE), 3))
##      chi2        df         p 
## 5.759e+01 3.000e+00 1.920e-12

Covariance scaling

Scaling each set by its own SDs returns the correlation and discards the magnitude information. Scaling all sets by a common reference (the natural population) keeps it.

sdx0 <- sd(at16$Delta_13C); sdy0 <- sd(at16$FT16)
sc <- function(x, y, lab) data.frame(set = lab, r = round(cor(x, y), 3),
  cov_raw = round(cov(x, y), 3),
  cov_ownSD = round(cov(x/sd(x), y/sd(y)), 3),
  cov_commonSD = round(cov(x/sdx0, y/sdy0), 3))
knitr::kable(rbind(
  sc(E$deltaC_mean_mean, E$dag_mean,   "29 edited"),
  sc(WC$deltaC_mean_mean, WC$dag_mean, "20 progenitors + Col-0"),
  sc(at16$Delta_13C, at16$FT16,        "248 natural (FT16)")), row.names = FALSE)
set r cov_raw cov_ownSD cov_commonSD
29 edited 0.376 0.902 0.376 0.028
20 progenitors + Col-0 0.144 1.876 0.144 0.058
248 natural (FT16) 0.381 12.262 0.381 0.381

Do not mean-standardise δ¹³C (Houle-style evolvability): its mean is negative on an arbitrary reference scale, so mean-scaled values are sign-inverted nonsense.

Relative variation (percentage)

δ¹³C has a negative mean on an arbitrary (VPDB) zero, so a signed CV is negative and uninterpretable. We therefore report 100 * SD / |mean| for δ¹³C, and a conventional CV for flowering time, which has a true zero.

relsd <- function(x) 100 * sd(x) / abs(mean(x))
cvpct <- function(x) 100 * sd(x) / mean(x)
cvrow <- function(lab, x, y) data.frame(
  set = lab, n = length(x),
  d13C_relSD_pct = round(relsd(x), 2),
  FT_CV_pct = round(cvpct(y), 2))

cvtab <- rbind(
  cvrow("29 edited",              E$deltaC_mean_mean,  E$dag_mean),
  cvrow("20 progenitors + Col-0", WC$deltaC_mean_mean, WC$dag_mean),
  cvrow("19 progenitors",         W$deltaC_mean_mean,  W$dag_mean),
  cvrow("248 natural (FT16)",     at16$Delta_13C,      at16$FT16),
  cvrow("261 natural (FT10)",     at10$Delta_13C,      at10$FT10))
knitr::kable(cvtab, row.names = FALSE)
set n d13C_relSD_pct FT_CV_pct
29 edited 29 1.44 24.49
20 progenitors + Col-0 20 1.40 43.59
19 progenitors 19 1.25 39.67
248 natural (FT16) 248 3.35 31.50
261 natural (FT10) 261 3.34 20.23 
c(d13C_ratio_progenitors_over_edited = round(relsd(WC$deltaC_mean_mean) /
                                             relsd(E$deltaC_mean_mean), 2),
  FT_ratio_progenitors_over_edited   = round(cvpct(WC$dag_mean) /
                                             cvpct(E$dag_mean), 2))
## d13C_ratio_progenitors_over_edited   FT_ratio_progenitors_over_edited 
##                               0.97                               1.78

Relative δ¹³C variation is essentially identical between edited lines and progenitors (ratio ≈ 0.97), while relative flowering-time variation is ~1.8× lower in the edited lines — the same conclusion as the F tests, without the mean shift that inflates the raw 32-fold variance ratio.

Only the progenitors-vs-edited comparison is condition-controlled (same chamber, same experiment). The natural panels were phenotyped at 16 °C and 10 °C, and CV depends strongly on condition — the same accessions give 31.5% at FT16 and 20.2% at FT10 — so chamber-vs-atlas CV ratios are not interpretable.

Measured vs imputed

imputed_wt&mut_dc13.csv holds separate wild-type and flc-mutant predictions for 306 accessions. For the edited lines that were actually measured it contains the measured values (fidelity r = 1), so imputation changes nothing there.

Scale warning. The two imputed columns are on different scales — mean wild-type −35.6‰ vs mean mutant −30.8‰, an offset of ~4.8‰ — which is why the analysis code divides them by different constants (−37.21 and −31.14). This is a plausible contributor to the wild-type/mutant non-overlap Reviewer 1 questioned in Fig. 3C.

c(mean_wt_imputed = round(mean(im$wt_dc13), 2), sd_wt = round(sd(im$wt_dc13), 3),
  mean_mut_imputed = round(mean(im$flc_mut_dc13), 2), sd_mut = round(sd(im$flc_mut_dc13), 3),
  offset = round(mean(im$wt_dc13) - mean(im$flc_mut_dc13), 2))

Flowering time vs fitness (Reviewer 2, comment 1b)

Reviewer 2 asked for the flowering-time/seed-weight relationship over the same lines as Fig. 3C. Source is the growth-chamber experiment (optimal treatment), not Uli’s δ¹³C run.

GC <- paste0("/Users/moisesexpositoalonso/Library/CloudStorage/",
             "GoogleDrive-moiexpositoalonso@berkeley.edu/Shared drives/MOI-LAB/PROJECTS/",
             "field_experiment_ranges/climate.change.evo.exp/field_prep_year1/crispr/growth chamber")
gc <- read.csv(file.path(GC, "wrangled_data_crispr.csv"))
sw <- read.csv(file.path(GC, "seed_weights.csv"))
gd <- merge(gc, sw, by = "NEW_ID")
gd$weight_w_paper <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gd$weight_w_paper))
gd$rSeedWeight <- gd$weight_w_paper - 0.3992667          # as in AtlasofPhenotypes.Rmd
gd$founder <- as.character(gd$founder)
gd$founder[is.na(gd$founder) | gd$founder == ""] <- "c"  # c = CRISPR, f = wild-type founder
gopt <- subset(gd, drought == "optimal")

# replicate wrangle_Expdata(): per line, drop NA seed weight, then average
wrangle <- function(dat) do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(dat$real_id), function(i) {
  t <- dat[dat$real_id == i, ]; t <- t[!is.na(t$rSeedWeight), ]
  if (!nrow(t)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(id = i, ft = mean(t$days_to_flowering, na.rm = TRUE),
             fit = mean(t$rSeedWeight, na.rm = TRUE)) }))
WTg  <- wrangle(subset(gopt, founder == "f"))
MUTg <- wrangle(subset(gopt, founder == "c"))

knitr::kable(rbind(stat(WTg$ft,  WTg$fit,  "wild type"),
                   stat(MUTg$ft, MUTg$fit, "CRISPR flc")), row.names = FALSE)
set n r p slope slope_SE cov sd_d13C sd_FT
wild type 39 -0.212 0.1950 0 0 -0.069 29.012 0.01
CRISPR flc 46 0.247 0.0976 0 0 0.059 18.438 0.01 
bb <- rbind(data.frame(ft = WTg$ft, fit = WTg$fit, g = "wt"),
            data.frame(ft = MUTg$ft, fit = MUTg$fit, g = "mut"))
round(summary(lm(fit ~ ft * g, data = bb))$coef, 5)   # ft:gwt = slope difference
##             Estimate Std. Error  t value Pr(>|t|)
## (Intercept)  0.01709    0.00480  3.56364  0.00062
## ft           0.00017    0.00010  1.79429  0.07650
## gwt          0.01625    0.00885  1.83703  0.06987
## ft:gwt      -0.00026    0.00012 -2.16871  0.03304
nWT <- sum(complete.cases(WTg$ft, WTg$fit))   # 2 wt lines lack flowering time: n = 39
zz <- (atanh(cor(MUTg$ft, MUTg$fit, use = "complete")) -
       atanh(cor(WTg$ft,  WTg$fit,  use = "complete"))) /
      sqrt(1/(nrow(MUTg) - 3) + 1/(nWT - 3))
c(fisher_z = round(zz, 3), p = round(2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(zz))), 4))
## fisher_z        p 
##   2.0810   0.0374
plot(WTg$ft, WTg$fit, pch = 19, col = "#4E9A6A",
     xlab = "Flowering time (days)", ylab = "Seed weight (g, paper-corrected)",
     main = "Flowering time vs fitness, growth chamber")
points(MUTg$ft, MUTg$fit, pch = 19, col = "#D7473A")
abline(lm(fit ~ ft, data = WTg),  col = "#4E9A6A", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(fit ~ ft, data = MUTg), col = "#D7473A", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", bty = "n", pch = 19, col = c("#4E9A6A", "#D7473A"),
       legend = c("wild type  r = -0.21, p = 0.195", "CRISPR flc  r = +0.25, p = 0.098"))

Neither correlation is individually significant, but they differ from each other (interaction p = 0.033; Fisher z = 2.08, p = 0.037 at full precision — the published “z = 2.07, p = 0.038” is the same test computed from the rounded correlations −0.21 and 0.25): the relationship reverses sign rather than disappearing. Over the same lines, fitness vs δ¹³C is r = −0.19 (p = 0.24) in wild types and r = 0.40 (p = 0.004) in edited lines — so WUE carries the stronger and only individually significant fitness association in the edited background.

Caveat. Flowering time in this chamber experiment spans 27.3–137.5 d in the edited lines, unlike 13.9–35.8 d in Uli’s δ¹³C panel. The two experiments are not the same set of lines, so the 32-fold variance collapse reported above applies to Uli’s panel only.

Supplement §VIII.2 — every number, in order

One chunk per claim, in the order the supplement makes them, so this section can be checked line-by-line against the text. Expected values from the current supplement are noted inline; everything reuses objects loaded above.

δ¹³C rank consistency between wild types and their flc counterparts

Expected: Spearman ρ = 0.66, p = 0.002; Pearson r = 0.77, p = 1×10⁻⁴, over the 19 wt–flc pairs.

Ep <- subset(d, label == "mut"); Wp <- subset(d, label == "wt")
Ep$acc <- firstnum(Ep$line); Wp$acc <- firstnum(Wp$line)
pw <- merge(Wp[, c("acc", "deltaC_mean_mean")], Ep[, c("acc", "deltaC_mean_mean")],
            by = "acc", suffixes = c("_wt", "_mut"))
c(n_pairs = nrow(pw))
## n_pairs 
##      19
suppressWarnings(   # ties -> approximate Spearman p
  cor.test(pw$deltaC_mean_mean_wt, pw$deltaC_mean_mean_mut, method = "spearman"))
## 
##  Spearman's rank correlation rho
## 
## data:  pw$deltaC_mean_mean_wt and pw$deltaC_mean_mean_mut
## S = 385.67, p-value = 0.002031
## alternative hypothesis: true rho is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##       rho 
## 0.6616938
cor.test(pw$deltaC_mean_mean_wt, pw$deltaC_mean_mean_mut)
## 
##  Pearson's product-moment correlation
## 
## data:  pw$deltaC_mean_mean_wt and pw$deltaC_mean_mean_mut
## t = 5.0221, df = 17, p-value = 0.0001046
## alternative hypothesis: true correlation is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.4910726 0.9082531
## sample estimates:
##       cor 
## 0.7728892

Measured phenotypes: r, slope, covariance, SD, CV per set

Expected: 19 paired edited r = 0.50, p = 0.030; 29 edited r = 0.38, p = 0.045, slope 4.58 ± 2.18, cov 0.90, SD 0.44 ‰ / 5.4 d, CV 1.44 % / 24.5 %; 20 progenitors + Col-0 r = 0.14, p = 0.55, slope 10.44 ± 16.94, cov 1.88, SD 0.42 / 30.8, CV 1.40 / 43.6; 248 natural (FT16) r = 0.38, p = 5.2×10⁻¹⁰, slope 8.63 ± 1.33, cov 12.26, SD 1.19 / 27.0, CV 3.35 / 31.5. (FT10 gives the same qualitative picture — Core statistics table above.)

statcv <- function(x, y, lab) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  cbind(stat(x, y, lab),
        CV_d13C_pct = round(relsd(x), 2), CV_FT_pct = round(cvpct(y), 2)) }

  statcv(E$deltaC_mean_mean,  E$dag_mean,    "29 edited"),
  statcv(WC$deltaC_mean_mean, WC$dag_mean,   "20 progenitors + Col-0"),
  statcv(at16$Delta_13C,      at16$FT16,     "248 natural (FT16)")), row.names = FALSE)

Variance F tests, measured

Expected: δ¹³C progenitors-vs-edited F = 0.91, p = 0.85; flowering time F = 32.35, p = 6.4×10⁻¹⁴; vs the 248 natural accessions δ¹³C F = 7.22, p = 6.8×10⁻⁸ and flowering time F = 24.82, p = 8.4×10⁻¹⁵. The relative-variation claims (δ¹³C CV 1.44 % vs 1.40 %, flowering-time CV 1.8-fold lower) are the CV columns above and the ratio pair in the Relative variation section.

vt <- function(x, y, lab) { v <- var.test(x, y)
  data.frame(comparison = lab, F = round(unname(v$statistic), 2),
             df = paste(v$parameter, collapse = ", "), p = signif(v$p.value, 2)) }

  vt(at16$FT16,           E$dag_mean,         "FT:   248 natural vs 29 edited")),

Traits vs fitness (seed weight, growth chamber)

Expected: flowering time vs seed weight r = −0.21, p = 0.195, n = 39 in wild types and r = 0.25, p = 0.098, n = 46 in edited lines; genotype × flowering-time interaction p = 0.033; Fisher z = 2.07, p = 0.038 (full precision gives 2.08 / 0.037 — the quoted 2.07 is z computed from the rounded correlations). The interaction model is in the previous section (ftfit_tests); cor.test drops the two wild-type lines with no flowering-time record, giving n = 39 of the 41.
